About the Position

3.5-year PhD at Newcastle University on empirical security assessment of AI decision engines in cyber-physical systems. Home fees covered plus £21,805 tax-free stipend. Deadline: 15 Oct 2026. Newcastle University invites applications for a PhD position in this area: Empirical Security Assessment of AI Decision Engines in Cyber-Physical Systems. Research areas covered include Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science. The role is based in Newcastle upon Tyne, United Kingdom. Funding is partial; financial support is listed as 2026-27/year (tax-free). Applications close 15 October 2026.

Tuition Coverage to Check

The advertised package covers Home-rate tuition. It should not be treated as full international-fee funding: confirm your fee status and any overseas-fee difference with the university before accepting.

Project Overview

Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven decision engines are increasingly embedded into cyber-physical systems (CPS) such as autonomous vehicles, smart grids, industrial control systems, robotics, healthcare devices, and intelligent transport infrastructure. While significant research has focused on improving the performance, efficiency, and autonomy of such systems, their empirical security assessment remains underdeveloped, representing a growing and critical gap.

Recent studies have highlighted vulnerabilities in learning-enabled CPS, demonstrating that small, carefully crafted perturbations can cause unsafe or malicious behaviours. However, much of the literature focuses either on theoretical attack construction or single-system evaluations, rather than on systematic, reproducible, and comparative empirical assessments across classes of AI decision engines. This PhD project aims to address this gap through the development of a rigorous empirical framework for evaluating the security robustness, failure modes, and operational risks of AI decision engines in cyber-physical environments.

Impact and Relevance

The proposed research directly addresses challenges faced by industries deploying AI-enabled CPS in safety-critical environments such as transportation, energy, and manufacturing. By providing empirical evidence rather than purely theoretical assurances, the project will support regulators, system designers, and security engineers in making informed deployment decisions. The outcomes are expected to influence both academic research and industrial best practices for trustworthy AI in cyber-physical systems.

Award Summary

  • 100% Home fees covered.
  • Minimum tax-free annual living allowance of £21,805 (2026-27 UKRI rates).
  • Award duration: 3.5 years.
  • Start date: 21 September 2026.
  • Number of awards: 1.
  • Sponsor: School of Computing.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • You must have, or expect to gain, a minimum 2:1 Honours degree or international equivalent in a relevant subject (including computing, mathematics, engineering, etc.).
  • Enthusiasm for research, ability to think and work independently, excellent analytical skills, and strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • The studentship covers fees at the Home rate (UK and EU applicants with pre-settled/settled status meeting residency criteria). International applicants are welcome but must cover the difference between Home and International fees.
  • Applicants whose first language is not English require an IELTS score of 6.5 overall with a minimum of 5.5 in all sub-skills.
  • International applicants may require an ATAS (Academic Technology Approval Scheme) clearance certificate prior to obtaining their visa.

Supervisor

Dr Mujeeb Ahmed

How to Apply

Apply through the University's Apply to Newcastle Portal:

  1. Register and select 'Create a Postgraduate Application'.
  2. Use 'Course Search' with programme code: 8050F.
  3. Research Area: Computing Science.
  4. Select 'PhD Computer Science (full time) - Computing Science'.
  5. In the 'Further Questions' section provide:
  • A Personal Statement (mandatory).
  • The studentship code COMP2177 in the 'Studentship/Partnership Reference' field.
  • Select 'Write Proposal' and type the research project title with your own statement.
